purpose: What ds-command-kernel::survey_media_address answers for a survey media reference: which of the three stored layouts it is, what it identifies, the object and thumbnail companion it resolves to, and the body a host sends to ds-brain's survey_media actions. The kernel replays this file in tests/survey_media_address_cases.rs and ds-web replays the identical copy through the vendored WASM, so no rule can be true on one host only.
source: ds-command-kernel/docs/contracts/survey-photo-outbox.md (Survey media address). The rules replace ds-web src/lib/api/survey-media-upload.ts (surveyMediaAddress) and are transcribed from ds-brain internal/handlers/survey_media.go (surveyMediaSegment, surveyMediaFileName, surveyMediaPath); the field app's layout is simple_notes/lib/src/core/entry_engine.dart.
note: Each case is the op WITHOUT the schema wrapper; `schema` overrides the default ds.survey-media-address/v1. `expected` is the parsed answer, or {"error": "<the exact Err string>"} when the reference or the request is refused. `refuses` names why, from the vocabulary below.

refusals.not_a_layout: The reference is not one of the three stored layouts.
refusals.bucket_qualified: A bucket prefix: a host cache key, not an object name.
refusals.escaped: A URL spelling: a percent escape, a query or fragment marker, or a control character.
refusals.separator: A Windows separator is not a path separator.
refusals.segment_charset: A segment is outside the gateway's segment character class.
refusals.segment_bound: A segment is longer than the gateway's 128-character bound.
refusals.file_name: The filename is a single dot or a double dot.
refusals.companion_bound: The _thunder.jpeg companion could not be a bounded object name.
refusals.malformed_request: The request itself is malformed; not a path refusal.

cases.why: The layout every DS browser upload has written since survey media existed: a project, the literal forms folder, a form, an entry and a file, with its thumbnail companion beside it.
The web layout must send exactly what ds-brain already accepts — four fields, no layout and no media_field — so an unreleased gateway keeps serving today's browser.
The reference ds-web's own fixtures carry: the same address under a projects/ root, which the old client parser refused outright.
A non-web layout must name itself so ds-brain recomposes the path it validated instead of trusting a client-sent string.
What simple_notes' entry_engine.dart uploads: projects/{p}/forms/{f}/{e}/{field}/{millis}_{index}.{ext}. Rotation was impossible for these photos until this layout was an address.
The field folder is the only part of a field_app path ds-brain cannot infer, so it travels as media_field beside the layout.
A _thunder.jpeg reference resolves to itself, because thumbnail_path_for never derives a thumbnail of a thumbnail.
A companion is a stored object like any other: the web layout addresses it with today's four-field body.
The companion rule replaces a final extension when there is one and appends when there is not; an extensionless capture still has one thumbnail name.
The segment rule admits dots — only a `..` is traversal — so a field named photo.front addresses normally.
Hosts hand over both spellings of the same object; a single leading slash is removed and nothing else about the stored name is rewritten.
ds-web's safeMediaFileName prefixes a field with an underscore, which the filename rule admits even though a folder segment may not begin with one.
128 characters is the gateway's segment bound, and the address must admit exactly what the gateway composes.
The longest original whose _thunder.jpeg companion is still a 255-character object name; one character more and the companion could not exist.
The defect's own sentence: a reference that stops at the entry identifies no stored object.
